Rca No. 157/2019 Unique Id No. : Dlct01-016103-2019 In the matter of: Shri Sunil Kumar Jain, S/o Late Multan Singh Jain, R/o F-1, Siddhi Vinayak Apartments, First Floor, Khasra No. 766, Burari, Delhi-110009. .........Plaintiff Versus Shri Mahesh Chander Gupta, S/o Late Dwarika Prashad Gupta, R/o H. No. Sk-37-38, Sindhora Kalan, Chowki No. 2, Near Shakti Nagar, Delhi-110007. .....Defendant Date of institution : 04.12.2019.
texts.facts: For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred by their original status. 2. Brief case of the plaintiff, as mentioned in the plaint, can be described herein as under:- RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 1 of 11 2.1 Plaintiff claims himself to be owner of shops No. 74 and 75, forming part of property No. 7255, situated at Ajindra Market, Prem Nagar, Delhi-110007 (hereinafter referred to as 'the suit property'), which were let out to the defendant at a monthly rent of Rs.10,000/- for a period of 11 months commencing from 01.07.2013 vide registered rent agreement dated 26.06.2013. It has been further stated that tenancy of the defendant came to an end in June, 2014. However despite repeated requests the defendant failed to vacate the tenanted/suit premises. Accordingly, a notice dated 23.06.2014, under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was served upon him but despite service of said notice defendant failed to vacate the tenanted/suit premises. Hence, plaintiff filed the present suit for possession, permanent injunction and recovery of damages/mesne profit. Written Statement 3.1 It has been stated in the written statement that father of defendant is the owner and in possession of the premises in question, who is carrying on his business of grocery shop under the name and style of his Sole Proprietorship Firm M/s Man Singh Multan Singh for last more than 22 years. It has been further stated that the prosecution was also initiated against the father of the defendant under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 on the basis of a sample lifted on 25.08.2021 from the premises in question and the father of defendant was convicted and sentenced on 30.11.2013 by the Court of Sh. Balwant Rai Bansal, ACMM, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi. It RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 2 of 11 has been further stated that the plaintiff is the friend of the defendant. It has been stated that for the past some time, the relations between the defendant and his father were not good and taking the undue advantage of said bad relations of defendant with his father, the plaintiff approached the defendant and assured that he would purchase the said shop from father of defendant or otherwise would get the premises in question vacated from the father of defendant by any manner and would provide peaceful and vacant possession of premises in question to the defendant and offered the defendant the tenancy of the premises in question. It has been further stated that believing the said false assurances and misrepresentation of the plaintiff, the rent agreement in question was executed between the parties but the said rent agreement was never acted upon as the plaintiff never handed over the possession of the premises in question to the defendant after getting it from the father of the defendant. Hence, the said rent agreement is null, void and illegal document. It has been further stated that the said rent agreement therefore never acted upon and the defendant has not paid any rent to the plaintiff and the plaintiff has filed the present suit only to extract money from the defendant. It has been further categorically stated that as such there is no relationship of landlord and tenant between the parties. 4. The decree of possession was passed vide order dated 20.11.2019 on the basis of admission of the defendant under order 12 rule 6 CPC, which has been challenged on the following grounds:- RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 3 of 11 (i) Ld. Though, the appellant had never admitted the respondent to be the owner of the suit property. (iii) Ld. (iv) Ld. Trial court erred in holding that defendant admitted that plaintiff is his landlord and he is in possession of the suit property in the capacity of tenant. (v) Ld. Trial court ignored the specific pleadings of the appellant in para No. 1 of the preliminary objections of the written statement that plaintiff never handed over possession of the premises in question to the defendant. Thus, the observations of Ld. Trial Court to the effect that defendant has admitted the plaintiff as his landlord and he is in possession of the suit property in the capacity of a Sunil Kumar Jain vs Mahesh Chander Gupta on 24 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175958709/ 2 tenant is factually incorrect and inconsistent with the pleadings of the appellant. RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 4 of 11 (vii) Ld. Trial Court has failed to examine the essential facts with respect to ownership and possession of the plaintiff over the suit property. The plaintiff, though, heavily relied upon the said rent agreement but failed to file any document before the Ld. Trial Court to show that he is the owner of the suit property or prior to execution of the said agreement he was in possession of the suit property. (viii) Ld. Trial Court has overlooked the fact that plaintiff has filed on record a GPA dated 20.08.1992 purportedly executed by one Guljar Singh Randhawa in his favour. The said GPA reflects that plaintiff had been made attorney with respect to shop No. 75 only and except the said document plaintiff has not been able to place any document to substantiate his claim of ownership and possession over the suit property. Though, the GPA with respect to shop No. 74 is in the name of Shri Rajiv Gupta, hence he was not competent to execute the rent agreement dated 26.06.2013 with respect to shop No. 74 and the same is void-ab-initio. (ix) Ld. No reply to the appeal was filed. However, it was orally argued by the counsel for the respondent that the Ld. Trial Court has rightly passed the impugned judgment / decree dated 20.11.2019. Therefore, the defendant has admitted that plaintiff is his landlord; that he is in possession of the suit property in the capacity of a tenant and that the rent agreement dated 26.06.2013 was executed between them. The rent agreement relied upon by the plaintiff is of dated 26.06.2013. The defendant has claimed the said rent agreement was got executed fraudulently by the plaintiff on misrepresentations and false assurances and actually his father is the owner and in possession of the suit property.

It was further contended by the Ld Counsel for appellant that the rent agreement dated 26.06.2013 is forged and fabricated as there is one more rent agreement which was executed by Mrs. Saloni Garg in favour of Soyam Singh Chauhan with respect to the shop no. Ld Counsel for appellant by pointing the above said document is making contradictory submissions. On one hand, it has been stated by the appellant that his father is owner of the suit property and on the other hand, he has relied upon above said document alleging that Mrs. Saloni Garg is the owner. The relevant portion of the said agreement is as under:- "Whereas the Landlord / First Party (Sh. Mahesh Chander Gupta) is the actual owner and in lawful possession of the shop no. 74 & 75, a part of the built up property bearing no. 7255 Situated at Ajindra Market, Prem Nagar, Delhi-110007 hereinafter called the property. 15. Here, I deem it appropriate to mention the judgment passed in the case of Vijaya Myne Vs. Satya Bhusan Kaura, reported in 142 (2007) DLT 483 (DB), the Division Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court has observed as under:- RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 9 of 11 "....... 12. The purpose and objective in enacting the provision like Order 12 Rule 6, CPC is to enable the Court to pronounce the judgment on admission when the admissions are sufficient to entitle the plaintiff to get the decree, in as much as such a provision is enacted to render speedy judgments and save the parties from going through the rigmarole of a protracted trial. The admissions can be in the pleadings or otherwise, namely in documents, correspondence etc. The admissions can even be constructive admissions and need not be specific or expressive which can be inferred from the vague and evasive denial in the written statement while answering specific pleas raised by the plaintiff. No doubt, for this purpose, the Sunil Kumar Jain vs Mahesh Chander Gupta on 24 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175958709/ Even a contrary stand taken while arguing the matter would be required to be ignored....." Reliance is placed upon in Vinay Kumar RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 10 of 11 Aggarwal Vs. Radha Rani Aggarwal 2018 SCC Online Del 6534. 17. The judgment relied upon by the appellant i.e. Karan Kapoor v. Madhuri Kumar; 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 567 is differentiable in the present facts and circumstances as herein the appellant has no document to show that he became the owner of the suit property.
